title: Productivity and Costs, Q3 2026 (revised) — the vintage the December FOMC reads
source: BLS: bls.gov/schedule/news_release/prod2.htm, read direct 2026-09-05, whose 2026 table's last row reads "Third Quarter 2026 (R) | Dec. 08, 2026 | 08:30 AM" — and independently on a structurally different BLS page the same session, bls.gov/schedule/2026/12_sched_list.htm, which reads "Tuesday, December 8, 2026 - 08:30 AM | Productivity and Costs (R) | Third Quarter 2026" and is internally consistent (it puts JOLTS on Tue Dec 1 and the Employment Situation on Fri Dec 4, so Dec 8 is a Tuesday). PROMOTED estimate->confirmed by this event's own never-assessed research: both grounds for the estimate label are discharged — the date is no longer carried secondhand from the productivity-costs-q3-2026-11-05 lane, and the no-self-confirm rule governs an adjacency DISCOVERED during a pulse, not an event's own initial research (precedent pce-2026-11-25, promoted by its own lane on the same reasoning). The 08:30 ET slot, previously recorded as not separately sourced, is now sourced on both pages. Caveat retained: plain curl 403s on every bls.gov HTML path and these pages served WebFetch only intermittently (the 11-05 lane got an empty body on 2026-09-05), so a BLS technical notice moving the slot reopens the date leg. checked 2026-09-05
notes: Custody, not information — that is this event's whole finding, and it corrects the premise it was filed under. The revised Q3 figures land 08:30 ET on DAY ONE of the Dec 8-9 FOMC (fomc-2026-12-09), inside the confirmed 2026-11-28 to 2026-12-10 blackout, so the committee has the number in the room and no Fed voice can discuss it. But five prelim->revised vintages pulled from the BLS news-release archive (Q3-2024, Q3-2025, Q4-2025, Q1-2026, Q2-2026) show nonfarm-business unit labor costs moving -1.1, 0.0, +1.6, -0.5, -0.1 percentage points of quarterly SAAR — real magnitude — while a one-quarter revision enters the 4-quarter rate at exactly 0.250pp per 1pp. ULC 4-quarter change reaches the Fed's 2% objective only at a Q3 SAAR of 3.41%; the central case is ~1.2% SAAR (1.45% y/y) and even the record's largest upward revision lifts it only to 1.85%. So the 2% question is decided on 2026-11-05, not here, unless the preliminary prints ULC SAAR >= 1.81%. Two structural facts: hours worked were revised 0.0pp in ALL five vintages (CES closes before the preliminary), and the channel is hourly compensation — the only revised nonfarm line in three of five, and the closest analog (Q3-2024, same Nov/Dec cadence) revised comp -1.1pp with output unrevised. The revision's own inputs are public by 2026-11-25 (BEA's Q3 GDP second estimate, proposed to this calendar as gdp-q3-2026-second-2026-11-25). Funding does not reach this date: H.R. 6500 (signed 2026-09-02) runs to 2026-12-11, three days later — the lapse branch belongs to the Q4 vintage. 2025 precedent for why that matters: the FY2026 lapse pushed the Q3-2025 preliminary to 2026-01-08 and its revision to 2026-01-29, so the December 2025 FOMC saw no Q3 productivity at all. Discovered during the productivity-costs-q3-2026-11-05 initial research; researched and promoted by its own lane 2026-09-05.
